'''Michael John Whelan''' [[Honorary Fellow of the Royal Microscopical Society|HonFRMS]] [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics|FInstP]] (2 November 1931 – 30 November 2024) was a British scientist.

== Education and career==
Whelan completed his PhD at [[Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge]] under the supervision of [[Peter Hirsch (metallurgist)|Peter Hirsch]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=Whelan, Prof. Michael John, (born 2 Nov. 1931), Professor of Microscopy of Materials, Department of Materials, University of Oxford, 1992–97, now Emeritus Professor; Fellow of Linacre College, Oxford, since 1967 {{!}} WHO'S WHO & WHO WAS WHO|language=en|doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.39498}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.aip.org/history-programs/niels-bohr-library/oral-histories/31625|title=Peter Hirsch|date=2015-02-11|access-date=2018-01-15}}</ref> He held research posts at the University of Cambridge until 1966 when he moved to the University of Oxford.<ref name=":0" /> As of 2011, Whelan was [[Emeritus Professor]] in the Department of Materials at the [[University of Oxford]], [[England]], and an Emeritus Fellow of [[Linacre College, Oxford]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Linacre College: Fellows | url=http://www.linacre.ox.ac.uk/Fellows | publisher=[[Linacre College, Oxford]] | accessdate=19 March 2012}}</ref>

== Awards ==
In 1976 he was elected as [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] and [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/michael-whelan-12516/|title=Michael Whelan|website=royalsociety.org|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-01-15}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> He and [[Archibald Howie]] won the 1988 [[Hughes Medal]] of the [[Royal Society]] "for their contributions to the theory of [[electron diffraction]] and [[microscopy]], and its application to the study of [[lattice defect]]s in [[crystal]]s".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://royalsociety.org/Content.aspx?id=3286|title=Hughes archive winners 1989 – 1902|publisher=[[The Royal Society]]|accessdate=20 January 2011}}</ref>  He also received the 1998 Distinguished Scientist Award in Physical Sciences from the [[Microscopy Society of America]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.microscopy.org/awards/past.cfm#scientist|title=Awards and Scholarships: Society Awards|publisher=Microscopy Society of America|accessdate=20 January 2011|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110319105103/http://www.microscopy.org/awards/past.cfm#scientist|archivedate=19 March 2011}}</ref> and the 1965 [[Institute of Physics#Awards|C.V. Boys Prize]] from the [[Institute of Physics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/career/moseley/medallists/page_38651.html|title=Moseley medal recipients|publisher=Institute of Physics|accessdate=20 January 2011}}</ref> In 2001 he was elected honorary fellow of the [[Royal Microscopical Society]].<ref name=":0" />  In 2011 he won the Gjønnes Medal in Electron Crystallography.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.materials.ox.ac.uk/peoplepages/whelan.html|title=Personal Homepages Oxford Materials|website=www.materials.ox.ac.uk|access-date=2018-01-15}}</ref>
